meta.probingQuestion: What happens to your mask when you're losing?

games.title: Single Leg — Make Partner Fall to Hands or Hips (Terminal)

meta.connection: When your guard gets passed, the mask cracks and something real shows. Getting passed on the mat and cracking under pressure are the same moment. You feel it in your body first.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, closed guard, and referee position. When your guard gets passed, something real slips out from under the mask, and you feel it in your body first. That crack is not failure, it is information. You get to notice what shows up and decide what to do with it.

slides.title: What happens to your mask when you're losing?

body.text: Single Leg — Make Partner Fall to Hands or Hips

items: The attacker wins when the defender's hips or hands touch the mat.
The defender wins by freeing his own leg from the attacker's grip.

body.text: Closed Guard Opening — Hands on Body

items: The top player wins by getting to his feet and opening the guard.
The bottom player wins by stopping the top player's win for 30 seconds. Then switch.

body.text: Referee Position Ride and Break Down

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps the bottom player broken down.
The bottom player wins when he stands up and faces the top player.

slides.title: What would you do?
slides.question: You're opening your partner's closed guard, and your hands drift up toward his head. What's the smart move?

options.text: Keep your hands on his hips and knees.
options.feedback: Right. Staying on the legs is what opens the guard, the same way pressure is what cracks the mask.

options.text: Reach for his head to control it.
options.feedback: Reaching for the head stalls the guard, not opens it.

options.text: Pull both hands back and reset your grip.
options.feedback: Resetting here loses your progress. Stay on the legs.
